key_insight: An iteration-dependent convex energy surrogate yields a minimizing-movement framework for parametric finite element approximation of anisotropic curve shortening with discrete energy dissipation.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports variationally consistent simulation of interface evolution and area-preserving geometric flows relevant to computational materials modeling.
method: Construct a smooth, convex surrogate that majorizes the anisotropic energy and matches it at the current iterate.
Solve a finite element minimization step, uniquely solvable for any positive time step when the current curve's parametric derivative is nonvanishing on every element.
Use convex splitting for strong anisotropy and a scalar constraint for area-preserving flows.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments show approximately expected convergence for smooth isotropic and weakly anisotropic cases, energy dissipation, and area preservation, while strong anisotropy produces facet-like profiles.
watch_item: Strongly anisotropic computations exhibit mesh-scale oscillations under grid refinement, warranting caution when interpreting fine-scale features.
paper_title: A minimizing-movement framework for parametric finite element approximation of anisotropic curve shortening flows
